title: The five mornings
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday, seven, the fifth morning. Fog again. The cover is the five drawings stacked: fog, clear, rain, clear-with-a-sleeve, fog. The owner says it's the same picture five times. Wood says look longer. She says she already does that.

panels.composition: The cover: five small drawings of the same view stacked top to bottom — fog, clear, rain with the sign lit, clear with a sleeve at the edge, fog.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing five small stacked drawings of the same town view in fog, clear light, rain, clear light and fog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet with five stacked drawings on its cover, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner's thumb on the fourth: the sleeve. She looks at Wood. Says nothing. Says nothing is her loudest.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner's thumb resting on one small drawing among five, her eyes lifted, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The five mornings facing the room. The strip did the view five times and it's the strip's first sequence. It doesn't know that word yet.

image.prompt: a small booklet in a wire rack with a cover of five stacked drawings, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Five mornings, one view: the first sequence. 'I already do that.'
